solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They can penetrate only 60 per cent of our puzzles

indicators.note: keeping only six of the ten letters means just the final stretch of the word survives

parts.note: the puzzles in this newspaper series are crosswords

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that only some of the paper's puzzles can be cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only 60 per cent of' keeps the last six of the ten letters of CROSSWORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades such as rapiers and sabres are weapons designed to pierce an opponent.

clue.text: They perform magic with one character finishing in hospital accommodation

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the hospital rooms, so this word signals a container

parts.note: patients are accommodated in wards
the Roman numeral for one is I
Z is the letter that finishes the alphabet

explanation.surface: Performers do conjuring tricks while one person recovers on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcerers and conjurors are said to work magic, the defining trait of the figure.

clue.text: River — a name for one in the country

parts.note: the Ural is the name of a river, so 'one' points back to the first word

explanation.surface: A river is named after something in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a name for one' means the name of a river, picking up 'River': the Ural flows from Russia into the Caspian Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes places and life found out in the countryside, away from towns.

clue.text: Thus church embraces German very quietly spoken

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first pieces wrap around the others

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Otto is a typical German man's name
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church welcomes a German who speaks very softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies V; the definition is just 'quietly spoken'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase, used in English, means in an undertone or under one's breath.

clue.text: Planetary satellite will be in astronomical list, obviously

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words astronomical list obviously

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes that a moon will naturally appear in the catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the large moons of Jupiter, discovered by Galileo, carries this name.

clue.text: Most serene maiden imprisoned in castle wickedly

indicators.note: a prisoner is shut inside, so one piece goes within the other
acting wickedly twists things, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A calm young woman is wickedly locked up in a castle, fairy-tale style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' scrambles CASTLE to CALEST, and M goes inside it. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and serene are synonyms, and here both are in the superlative degree.

clue.text: Actress left before fiddler rolled up

indicators.note: in a down entry, rolling up reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: the emperor Nero supposedly fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: An actress leaves just before a violinist arrives in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is a celebrated Italian film star, the example the clue points to.

clue.text: What redevelopment could make nicer: tiny downtown area

indicators.note: redeveloping rebuilds and rearranges, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Planners hope regeneration will make a cramped central district more pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The densely built central part of a city is commonly called by this term.

clue.text: That lot joining everybody in London thoroughfare

parts.note: them refers to that group of people
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A crowd of people all join together in a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MALL is the grand avenue running from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial road leading to Buckingham Palace is a famous street in the capital.

clue.text: Strict police policy? It could be to clear zone when monarch enters

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the other
suggests the letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Police clear an area before a royal visit, as an example of strict policing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges TO CLEAR ZONE into ZEROTOLANCE, and ER 'enters' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a policing approach that punishes every minor offence without leniency.

clue.text: Mythical creature associated with work by English novelist

parts.note: a troll is a creature of Scandinavian folklore
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A fantasy monster features in a book by an English author.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Trollope wrote the Barsetshire novels; 'English' looks like it describes him but supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a prolific Victorian writer of fiction, so he is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Wisdom maybe shown by invader

definitions.meaning: ... Wisdom was a British slapstick comedian, so his first name is meant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wisdom' looks like a quality, but the capital hides Sir Norman Wisdom, a much-loved British film comic.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic's first name, and also a member of the people who conquered England.

clue.text: Dangerous personality could make cop shy

indicators.note: suggests the letters can be made into another word

explanation.surface: A dangerous person could make even a police officer timid.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychopathic, mentally unstable person is colloquially given this label.

clue.text: Cow adored being unconventional — see it in a tree!

indicators.note: behaving unconventionally means the letters break their normal order

explanation.surface: A much-loved cow behaves oddly and is spotted up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber of the cedar is found inside that tree, so you would see it in one.

clue.text: The heartless bishop needs the Good Book — no leader, dreadful!

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its central letter, which is removed

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the Bible is often called the Good Book

explanation.surface: A bishop in need of a Bible finds it starts badly and exclaims his dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' cuts the H from THE to give TE; 'no leader' drops the B of BIBLE to leave IBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrible and dreadful are synonyms meaning extremely bad.

clue.text: No longer devoid of drink, being able to supply juice again?

definitions.meaning: a glass refilled with drink has been topped up

definitions.text: being able to supply juice again?
definitions.meaning: juice is slang for electric power, as from a battery restored

explanation.walkthrough: 'juice' looks like fruit drink but means electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses are recharged when refilled, and batteries when restored to power.

clue.text: US city in desert perhaps with one personality

parts.note: a desert is an example of a sandy expanse
the Roman numeral for one is I
ego is one's sense of self or personality

explanation.surface: An American city lies in a desert, along with one notable character.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large city in southern California, an instance of a US city.

clue.text: Old boy, somehow I race around — is the exercise this?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece
means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil runs about wondering whether this counts as a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I RACE to AERIC, which goes 'around' OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise like running that raises breathing and heart rate is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Unconventional, like a suspended copper?

definitions.meaning: a police officer suspended from duty is not out walking the beat

explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal but is slang for a police officer, whose route is a beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something quirky or eccentric departs from the usual rhythm or norm.

clue.text: Wolf gets round yard to enter sheepfold?

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the enclosure, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for sheep or birds
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A wolf prowls around a farmyard hoping to get into the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a North American wild dog sometimes called the prairie wolf.

clue.text: Violent words may be heard in Far Eastern attacks

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: raids by people from Thailand, in the Far East, would be Thai raids

explanation.surface: Angry words are overheard during assaults in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry outbursts of speech are fierce, violent words.

clue.text: Boring feature of cricket practice

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
runs are how cricket scores are made

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that cricket practice is a tedious affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal held before the real thing is called by this phrase.

clue.text: End of life before long after it's been set up?

definitions.text: End of life before long after it's been set up?

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means read from bottom to top
the last letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: soon means before long

explanation.surface: Death will follow soon after the hangman's rope is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: E from 'life' plus SOON reads upwards as the answer; the whole clue also describes the hangman's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman's loop brings about the end of a life once it has been rigged.

clue.text: Insincere praise less exciting, given to unknown character

parts.note: flatter means duller, less lively
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Praise that is less exciting is lavished on an unknown person.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive compliments not truly meant are a form of buttering up.

clue.text: Vehicles the reverse of stylish

indicators.note: the word is read backwards

parts.note: smart means stylish

explanation.surface: Some vehicles are far from fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: These are passenger vehicles running on rails in city streets.

clue.text: Frightful rogue banned, so watch out

indicators.note: frightful means terrible, a mess, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A terrible villain has been barred, so people should take care.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay alert and wary of danger is to keep watch.

clue.text: A big game involving detectives in searching examination

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives are drawn into a major sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a top-level international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive trial of quality or worth is a crucial, searching examination.

clue.text: Stop Society being restricted by one sort of believer

indicators.note: the piece is held inside the other, so it is a container

parts.note: a deist believes in a creator who does not intervene

explanation.surface: A believer tells a religious society to stop interfering.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or refrain from an action.
